weather_report:
West Perth wakes to a lucid, wintry brightness: the kind of clear morning where shadows are sharp and the air tastes clean. The sky is swept free of cloud, a polished blue dome that makes colours pop and the city edges look newly drawn. It feels cool in the shade but kind on the skin when you stand in the sun, a gentle warmth seeping through the chill without any heaviness.

The day holds to this clarity into the early afternoon, bright and uncomplicated. Sunshine will be generous, the UV modest by summer standards yet still spirited enough to warrant sunglasses and a dab of sunscreen if you linger outdoors. Light layers suit it best—a soft knit over a tee, something you can shrug off as the sun takes hold—and a brimmed hat won’t go amiss. It’s a good day for simple pleasures: a quiet walk up to Kings Park for a look over the river, errands done on foot, lunch in a sunlit courtyard, or airing the house while you read by an open window. Expect a pleasing, unhurried mood to the hours ahead, all clean lines and blue distance.
